message.content:
I'm doing a gap analysis for KasirKu (a Next.js/Supabase multi-tenant POS+finance SaaS at G:\PROJECT1\KasirKu) against a reference HTML prototype called "AkunPro" that the user wants to use as a design+functionality blueprint for a possible "sell the finance/accounting module separately" product.

I need you to check whether these specific features/pages currently exist in the KasirKu codebase (search under src/app/business/[businessId]/ or wherever the dashboard routes live), and briefly summarize what exists for each (file path + one-line description of current behavior). Report "MISSING" if genuinely absent.

1. **Invoice/Nota generation** — creating a printable invoice/quote for catering/event orders (client name, line items, DP/down payment, due date, print) — separate from POS receipts.
2. **Notifikasi/Reminder center** — a single page or widget aggregating: hutang (payables) due soon, unpaid invoices, upcoming THR, unpaid payroll, contract-expiring employees.
3. **Kas Harian** — a simplified non-accounting cash in/out log meant for a cashier with no bookkeeping knowledge (separate from the full Jurnal/manual journal entry page).
4. **Rekap Absensi Bulanan** — a monthly attendance summary/rollup page (Hadir/Izin/Sakit/Alpha counts per employee for a whole month), distinct from daily attendance.
5. **Lembur (overtime)** — check whether overtime is currently just a manual nominal field on the payslip, or whether there's an hours × hourly-rate × multiplier (1.5x/2x per Indonesian labor law) calculator.
6. **THR (Tunjangan Hari Raya)** — check whether it's a manual nominal field, or auto-calculated from tenure (masa kerja) per PP No. 36/2021 rules.
7. **Payroll komponen gaji settings** — check whether there's a configurable settings panel for allowances (tunjangan jabatan/makan/transport, toggle on/off) and deductions (BPJS Kesehatan %, BPJS Ketenagakerjaan %, kasbon/loan, alpha deduction) — or whether payroll math is simpler/hardcoded.
8. **Rekonsiliasi Rekening** — check the CURRENT implementation detail: is it a simple book-balance-vs-statement-balance snapshot tool (one number vs one number), or does it break down by payment method (Tunai/QRIS/EDC) comparing POS-recorded totals against bank-recorded totals per method, with a computed merchant/MDR fee percentage per method?
9. **Global period switcher** — is there a single "active period" (month/year) selector that syncs across multiple report pages, or does each report page have its own independent period filter?
10. **Export to Excel (bulk, all data at once)** and **print-friendly styling** for reports (slip gaji, invoice, laporan) — do these exist anywhere in the codebase already (e.g. via a browser print stylesheet or a library)?

Also tell me: what is the current brand/visual design system for the dashboard (primary color, font, layout pattern — sidebar nav groups etc.)? Check src/app/globals.css and the dashboard shell component (something like dashboard-shell.tsx).

Report back concisely, organized by the 10 numbered items above plus the design system question. For each item state: EXISTS (with file path + brief description) or MISSING, and keep it factual — I'll do my own synthesis after your report.

- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

Confirmed. I have everything needed for the report.

## Gap Analysis: KasirKu vs AkunPro Blueprint

**1. Invoice/Nota generation (catering/event) — MISSING**
No dedicated invoice/quote builder anywhere in `src/app/business/[businessId]/`. Searches for "invoice", "nota pesanan", "down payment/DP", "generate invoice" turned up nothing beyond POS receipt printing (`transactions/[transactionId]/receipt/page.tsx`, `ticket-reports/[transactionId]/receipt/page.tsx`), which are simple paid-in-full POS receipts — no client name, DP tracking, or due date fields exist anywhere.

**2. Notifikasi/Reminder center — MISSING**
No aggregating notification/reminder page or widget. There's no employee contract-end-date field at all (`kontrak`/`contract_end` search returned nothing), so "contract-expiring employees" can't even be computed today. Related data exists in isolated pages (receivables aging in `receivables/page.tsx`, purchases/hutang in `purchases/page.tsx`) but nothing surfaces them together as reminders.

**3. Kas Harian (simplified cash log) — MISSING**
There's an "Arus Kas Harian" chart on the main dashboard (`src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/page.tsx`, line ~171) but it's just a read-only SVG line chart of monthly revenue vs. expense by day — not an input log. The only ways to record cash movement are the full double-entry `Jurnal Transaksi` (`accounting/jurnal/page.tsx`, `add-journal-form.tsx`) and the Finance page's expense form (`finance/add-expense-form.tsx`), both of which assume bookkeeping literacy (accounts/categories). No cashier-friendly "in/out" log exists.

**4. Rekap Absensi Bulanan — EXISTS (embedded, not standalone)**
`src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/attendance/page.tsx` (lines 69–159) includes a "Rekap Bulan Ini" section beneath the daily attendance grid — per-employee Hadir/Izin/Sakit/Alpa counts for the month-to-date, computed inline. It's not a separate/standalone monthly report page, and it's capped to the currently-viewed month via the date navigator, not a dedicated month picker.

**5. Lembur (overtime) — Manual nominal only, MISSING calculator**
`payroll/[payslipId]/lembur-thr-form.tsx` and `payroll/actions.ts` (`updatePayslipExtras`) store `lembur_amount` as a single free-typed Rupiah number. No hours field, no hourly-rate derivation, no 1.5x/2x multiplier logic anywhere in the payroll code.

**6. THR — Manual nominal only, MISSING tenure calculation**
Same form/action as above: `thr_amount` is a plain manual number field. No masa-kerja/tenure lookup, no PP 36/2021 proportional calculation. Employees table only tracks `daily_rate` and `active` (from `createPayslip` in `payroll/actions.ts`) — no hire-date-driven tenure logic feeds into payroll.

**7. Payroll komponen gaji settings — MISSING (simple/hardcoded, not configurable)**
`payroll/[payslipId]/add-adjustment-form.tsx` + `addPayslipAdjustment` in `payroll/actions.ts` only offer two free-form types: "tunjangan" (allowance) and "potongan" (deduction), each with a user-typed label and nominal amount, entered per-payslip. There is no settings panel anywhere (checked `settings/page.tsx` — no payroll section) for predefined allowance types (jabatan/makan/transport toggles), BPJS Kesehatan/Ketenagakerjaan percentages, kasbon/loan tracking, or automatic alpha-day deductions. Base pay is simply `daily_rate × hadir_count`.

**8. Rekonsiliasi Rekening — EXISTS, and already the more sophisticated version**
Two distinct implementations exist:
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/finance/page.tsx` (lines 138–413) + `merchant-fee-input.tsx` + `add-reconciliation-form.tsx`: breaks reconciliation down **by payment method** (Tunai/Kartu/QRIS), computing POS-recorded totals per method, a per-method configurable merchant fee % (`merchant_fees` table via `MerchantFeeInput`), estimated net after fee, actual amount received (manually logged), and the variance — exactly the richer version described in your question.
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/accounting/rekonsiliasi/page.tsx`: a separate, simpler general-ledger-account reconciliation tool — single book-balance (from `journal_entries`) vs. single statement-balance snapshot per asset account, with history. This is the "one number vs one number" style tool, coexisting alongside the per-method one.

**9. Global period switcher — MISSING (each report page has its own independent filter)**
`reports/period.ts` provides shared `Period` type/helpers (`parsePeriod`, `getPeriodRange`), but each page (`reports/page.tsx`, `reports/laba-rugi/page.tsx`, `reports/cogs/page.tsx`, `reports/price-trend/page.tsx`, `ticket-reports/page.tsx`) reads its own `?period=`/`?from=`/`?to=` from its own `searchParams` independently — selecting a period on one report does not carry over to another. Note also `finance/page.tsx` defines its own separate, incompatible `Period` type (`"today"|"week"|"month"|"all"`, no "custom") — not even using the shared `period.ts` helper.

**10. Export to Excel & print-friendly styling — PARTIALLY EXISTS**
- CSV export (Excel-openable, UTF-8 BOM) exists for: sales reports (`reports/export/route.ts`), ticket reports (`ticket-reports/export/route.ts`), and product list import/export (`products/export/route.ts`). These are per-report/per-page CSV exports, not a single "export everything at once" bulk feature.
- Print-friendly styling exists via Tailwind's `print:` variant + `window.print()`, used on: payroll slip (`payroll/[payslipId]/page.tsx` + `print-button.tsx`), POS transaction receipt (`transactions/[transactionId]/receipt/page.tsx` + `print-button.tsx`), ticket receipt (`ticket-reports/[transactionId]/receipt/page.tsx`), and member card (`members/[memberId]/card/page.tsx`). The shared `dashboard-shell.tsx` also hides sidebar/topbar via `print:hidden`/`print:p-0`. Report pages (`reports/page.tsx`, etc.) have no print styling — they rely on CSV export instead. Since there's no invoice feature, there's no invoice print stylesheet either.

## Design System (dashboard shell + globals.css)

- **Primary brand color**: `src/app/globals.css` (lines 14–24) defines a "Majoo-style bright green" palette, `--color-brand-500: #00a651` as primary, with a 50–900 scale (`brand-600: #00944a` used most for buttons/active states).
- **Font**: `body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; }` (globals.css line 37), though `--font-sans`/`--font-mono` are wired to Geist fonts via the theme block (Next.js font optimization) — worth confirming which actually wins in practice, but body explicitly forces Arial/Helvetica as fallback-first.
- **Layout pattern**: `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/dashboard-shell.tsx` — a fixed left sidebar (256px/`w-64` desktop, slide-out drawer on mobile) + sticky topbar + main content area capped at `max-w-6xl`. Background is light gray (`#F4F6F9`) with white cards/shadow-sm panels.
- **Sidebar nav groups** (`buildNavGroups`, lines 52–152): collapsible accordion groups — "Keuangan" (Dashboard, Laporan, Laba Rugi, COGS, HPP Calculator, Keuangan/reconciliation, Riwayat Transaksi, Riwayat Shift), "Akuntansi" (Daftar Akun, Laba Rugi Akrual, Jurnal, Neraca, Arus Kas, Target vs Aktual, Perubahan Modal, Transfer Kas/Bank, Rekonsiliasi Rekening, Tutup Buku), "Operasional" (varies by business type: Produk, Bahan Baku, Meja for F&B; Check-in/Laporan Tiket/Anggota for tiket businesses; Pelanggan, Piutang, Pembelian & Hutang, Supplier, Aset Tetap), "SDM" (Karyawan, Kelola Kasir, Absensi, Payroll), "Lainnya" (Pengaturan, Aktivitas). Groups auto-expand based on active route; icons via `lucide-react`.
- Business type drives nav content (`fnb`/`retail`/`tiket` union type), and the shell also renders a billing past-due banner inline when applicable.
